kind: Phase 12's last confirmed MAJOR. Plan:2884-2888 mandates 'run Task 13.1's scripted e2e twice — once with the router in the loop, once with --no-router — and assert the same terminal state, the same item dispositions, and the same commit set', explicitly so that 'the identical process runs without the router' is true rather than aspirational. What shipped is a python unit test comparing config dicts, env dicts and argv lists — it never runs the e2e — plus an artifact whose two arms are THE SAME COMMAND run twice.
authoredBy: orchestrator — from docs/build/artifacts/phase-gates-12-13-15-findings.md phase 12 MAJOR 1, plus TWO facts the orchestrator verified itself that make the defect worse than recorded (below).
bindings: Repairs row 12.1-G5. Also closes the phase-13 MINOR 'the router fail-soft property is not exercised: the metrics seam is omitted, not stubbed against a dead endpoint', which is the same hole seen from the other side. Phase 12's gate can be re-run once this lands.
verifiedAgainstHead: THE RECORDED DEFECT. docs/build/artifacts/12.1-g5-equivalence.md records arm A as `CONDUCTOR_OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8088/v1 node --test conductor/tests/e2e.test.ts` and arm B as the same command with `:8080/v1`. `grep -rn CONDUCTOR_OPENAI_BASE_URL conductor/ scripts/` returns ZERO hits — the variable is read by nothing, so the two arms are byte-identical invocations. The named driver conductor/tests/e2e-g5.test.ts does not exist.

ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED, FACT 1, and it makes the defect deeper: `grep -rn 'fetchMetricsSummary|router' conductor/tests/e2e.test.ts` returns NOTHING. The e2e has no router touchpoint whatsoever. `reportArgs()` passes no `metrics` field and `handleReport` does `input.metrics === undefined ? null : await input.metrics()`, so adapter/router-client.ts fetchMetricsSummary is never called by any scenario. Even a correctly-wired env var would have changed nothing: the equivalence is a tautology on two counts, not one.

ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED, FACT 2, and it constrains the fix: conductor/tests/router-client.test.ts:5 states 'the unit tests need neither the C++ llama-router nor a model', and a fresh detached worktree has no submodules and therefore no built router (acceptance row 3 is already environmental for exactly this reason). A test that SPAWNS llama-router must therefore NOT join the node suite's default run, or every fresh-checkout verification starts requiring a C++ build.

adapter/router-client.ts:197 fetchMetricsSummary(routerCfg, log?) is strictly fail-soft by contract — null on any failure, never a throw. That is what makes an arm with no router listening a legitimate arm rather than a crash.

The llama-router binary exists at .out/build/clang-relwdebinfo/llama-router and its usage is `llama-router --config <path> --schema <path>` — both required, no defaults and no search path. It needs no model to start and no live upstream to serve its own endpoints.

Row 13.1-router-absent-fail-soft already states the property the WITHOUT arm must show: 'the whole file completes with NO router listening: router-client.fetchMetricsSummary is left UNSTUBBED against a dead endpoint, returns null without throwing, the report renders a metrics-unavailable line rather than crashing or blocking, and no scenario's outcome differs'. It is currently unmet because the seam is omitted rather than exercised.
specGaps: G5-SG-1 (the WITH arm cannot live in the node suite). Spawning the C++ router from conductor/tests/*.test.ts would make the default suite depend on a built binary that a fresh worktree does not have. RESOLUTION: the equivalence driver is a SEPARATE script producing an artifact, the way the plan's 'run it twice and assert' reads. The node suite keeps the WITHOUT arm — which needs no router — as an ordinary test.

G5-SG-2 (what 'the same' means is fixed by the plan, not by the author). The compared facts are exactly three: the same terminal state, the same item dispositions, the same commit set. The metrics section of the report legitimately DIFFERS between arms — that is the point of having two — and is not part of the comparison.

G5-SG-3 (the artifact must not be able to become a tautology again). Whatever the driver records must make two IDENTICAL commands visibly wrong. The recorded arms differed only by an env var nothing reads, and nothing in the artifact's own shape objected.
G5-SG-4 (out of scope). No model, ever. The e2e's fake SDK stays the only fake. Do not touch the C++ router's source.

assertions.text: the e2e actually REACHES adapter/router-client.ts: reportArgs passes a `metrics` function, so handleReport calls it instead of short-circuiting on `undefined`. Asserted by observing the call — a report whose metrics section exists because the seam ran, not because the field was absent. Without this row the two G5 arms cannot differ in any observable way, which is why the shipped equivalence was vacuous

row 13.1-router-absent-fail-soft, finally met: with NO router listening, fetchMetricsSummary is left UNSTUBBED against a dead endpoint, returns null WITHOUT THROWING, the report renders a metrics-unavailable line, and no scenario's terminal state, item disposition or commit set differs from a run with the seam omitted entirely. This arm needs no C++ binary and belongs in the node suite (G5-SG-1)

an equivalence driver exists that runs the pipeline TWICE — once against a REAL llama-router process it starts (`--config` and `--schema`, no model, no live upstream required) and once with nothing listening — and compares the three facts plan:2884-2888 names: the same terminal state, the same item dispositions, the same commit set. It is NOT the same command twice: the two invocations differ in something the code actually reads, and the driver fails if the router arm's router was never contacted

the WITH arm proves the router was genuinely in the loop rather than merely running: the driver asserts the router process served the metrics request — observed on the router's side or on a non-null MetricsSummary reaching the report, never inferred from the process being alive. A router that started and was never contacted is the same tautology in a new costume

the recorded artifact makes the shipped defect impossible to repeat: it carries both arms' actual invocations AND the evidence each arm was distinct (the router arm's contacted-router proof, the without arm's null metrics), and a check rejects an artifact whose two arms are byte-identical commands or whose difference is a variable no source file reads. `grep -rn CONDUCTOR_OPENAI_BASE_URL conductor/ scripts/` returning zero hits is what made the previous artifact worthless while looking complete (G5-SG-3)

the node suite still needs neither the C++ llama-router nor a model, as conductor/tests/router-client.test.ts:5 promises: `bash scripts/test-conductor.sh` passes in a fresh detached worktree with no submodules and no built binary. Asserted so that closing G5 does not quietly make every fresh-checkout verification depend on a C++ build (G5-SG-1)
